title: Source Quality and Authority: Visual Guide
outline: Title: Source Quality and Authority: Visual Guide

1. Fetched To Trusted | a six-stage pipeline over 10,000 fetched responses, two stages already taught (URL canonicalization, extraction discard) and four new, each tappable off and labelled REMOVES, REORDERS or LABELS | acquisition ends at 10,000 fetches and corpus quality begins there, judging each page against the other pages rather than alone — and a graph prior and credibility labels remove nothing at all

2. PageRank By Hand | the A-to-B-and-C, B-to-C, C-to-A graph iterated live with a damping slider, printed arithmetic per node, and a dangling-page mode toggled between untreated and teleport-redistributed | PR(u) = (1-d)/N + d times the sum of PR(v)/L(v) gives A 0.333, B 0.192, C 0.475 on the first iteration at d=0.85, the vote is split by out-degree, and an untreated dangling page leaks probability until the vector is no longer a distribution

3. Spam Signal Stack | four sliders over the worked page (1,700 templated words of 2,000, 120 phrase repeats, 0.40 link density, 5,000 siblings) scored against three source types with per-type tolerances | no single threshold proves spam and the same features mean different things on a doorway page and an API reference, so probabilistic junk is downranked or quarantined while hard-reject stays reserved for malware, empty extraction and policy violations

4. Keep Or Drop | one four-member cluster (original paper, author copy, news summary quoting 60%, scraped copy) re-judged under three corpus purposes, plus a length slider showing a shared 100-word footer against a fixed 20% similarity threshold | dedup is a policy not a threshold — declare the equivalence class first, keep one serving representative with alternates and provenance recorded, and make thresholds length-aware because a footer is a third of a short notice and nothing in a manual

5. Credible For What | three sources scored on seven separately stored signals, reweighted live by claim type so the ranking flips, plus a stepper turning N republishing sites into one evidence lineage | credibility is claim-relative rather than a permanent domain score, and corroboration requires independent lineages, so five sites copying one press release are one confirmation
